selectedFunctions.label: OctoSwap add liquidity
warnings: Static deployment/source/ABI metadata only; no persistent runtime identity, funding, liquidity, execution, financial safety or complete-workflow assurance. Exact grants, independent policies, pauses and canonical calldata/value validation remain required.

Chain 143 is Monad mainnet. ETH-named payable parameters/functions mean native MON, not Ethereum ETH; WETH() is immutable WMON 0x3bd359c1119da7da1d913d1c4d2b7c461115433a. Only addLiquidityETH, swapExactETHForTokens and swapETHForExactTokens accept native value; every nonpayable selected function requires zero native value. addLiquidityETH and exact-output native swaps refund unused MON to msg.sender, whose recipient code must accept it.

This non-proxy Classic router binds immutable factory 0xce104732685b9d7b2f07a09d828f6b19786cda32 and pair init-code hash 0x1305842295bb388975eec146e164811bee4ac15606baa6205d5749e933f26762. Token path elements select factory-derived pairs, not arbitrary targets/selectors/bytes; router uses fixed pair.swap with empty callback bytes. Universal Router, multicall, CL router/position manager, permit, direct pair mint/burn, callbacks and admin capabilities are not admitted.

ERC20 input and both liquidity assets are pulled from msg.sender directly to the derived pair using prior router allowance; LP removal pulls caller LP shares to pair and burns them atomically. Recipient to is caller-selected and can differ from owner/caller. No delegated owner parameter or authorization is inferred. Never pre-fund pairs or router: pair mint/burn account for surplus balances and all LP shares already at the pair, so unrelated donations can alter results.

Swaps require a path of at least two tokens, active pairs and sufficient reserves. Native input paths start with WMON and native output paths end with WMON. Set intentional amountOutMin/amountInMax and deadline (Unix seconds, inclusive); all quantities use token base units. Exact-input outputs floor and exact-output inputs round up per hop; library applies 997/1000 input multiplier (0.3% pair fee). Fees, price movement and price impact remain economic risks, not guarantees.

Liquidity uses current reserve ratio and expiry. On addLiquidity, only the reduced/optimal side is checked against its minimum; the full desired side is not independently minimum-checked. Empty pools use both desired amounts directly without enforcing either minimum. There is no minimum-LP-share parameter. Initial pair mint permanently locks 1000 units; floor rounding and feeTo protocol LP minting affect shares/payout. removeLiquidity checks both gross pair-returned amounts, not net receipts after token taxes.

Only ordinary amount-preserving token paths/liquidity are selected. Rebasing, fee-on-transfer, denylisted, malicious or transfer-restricted assets can fail or give misleading output guarantees; supporting-fee variants that use router-wide balances and all permit variants remain excluded. Token contracts and native recipient callbacks are unavoidable configured/data-derived dependencies, not an isolation claim. No protocol KYC check appears in these router entrypoints, but app/jurisdiction/token restrictions and eligibility are not attested.

Security & Audits

Security is a top priority at OctoSwap. To ensure user safety and protocol reliability, we've based our core infrastructure on the Uniswap v2 and v3 core and periphery contracts—some of the most battle-tested and thoroughly audited smart contracts in the DeFi space.

Audits​

Our core infrastructure is based on these audited contracts:

Battle-Tested Security

These smart contracts have processed over $2 trillion in trading volume with no critical exploits in the audited core protocols.

Ongoing & Future Audits​

Protocol Customizations: While our core trading logic and liquidity pools are based on Uniswap, any custom features, integrations, or additions unique to OctoSwap will undergo additional independent security audits.

Transparency: As new audits are completed, we will publish the reports here for the community's review.

# OctoSwap Classic-V1 Periphery Changes (Uniswap V2 Periphery)

Comparison between `octoswap-v1-periphery` and original `uniswap/v2-periphery`.

## Contract Changes

### OctoswapRouter.sol (UniswapV2Router02.sol)
- **Line 12**: Contract name `UniswapV2Router02` → `OctoswapRouter`

### libraries/UniswapV2Library.sol
- **Line 24**: Init code hash `0x96e8ac4277198ff8b6f785478aa9a39f403cb768dd02cbee326c3e7da348845f` → `0x1305842295bb388975eec146e164811bee4ac15606baa6205d5749e933f26762`

## Unchanged Components

- **Base contracts**: All base contracts identical (100% match)
- **Interfaces**: All interface files identical (100% match)
- **Libraries**: All library files except UniswapV2Library.sol identical (100% match)

## Dependencies

All dependencies byte-for-byte identical to Uniswap V2 Periphery:
- `@uniswap/lib`: 4.0.1-alpha
- `@uniswap/v2-core`: 1.0.0

---

## Summary

All changes are purely branding-related (contract name only). All functional code, including routing logic, liquidity management, swap calculations, library functions, Solidity versions, and compiler optimization settings remain 100% identical to the original Uniswap V2 Periphery contracts. The init code hash change reflects the renamed core pair contract.
